content.summary: Reasoning engine for cognitive cycle. Deductive/inductive/abductive/analogical inference, causal analysis, hypothesis formation with Bayesian model selection (BIC/AIC), evidence evaluation with Bayesian evidence weighting (v2.18.0 B-3), belief updating, goal decomposition, plan generation. Dynamic search budget, predictive coding/FEP, curiosity-driven reprioritization. Protocol: AIAP V1.0.0.
content.description: Reasoning sub-module called by main.aisop.json Reasoning node. 9 nodes: PremiseExtraction -> InferenceEngine -> CausalAnalysis -> HypothesisFormation -> EvidenceEvaluation -> BeliefUpdate -> GoalDecomposition -> PlanGeneration -> ReasoningOutput. Handles all deliberative processing including multi-step inference chains, causal modeling, and action planning. Uses google_search and web_browser tools when factual grounding is needed. Features dynamic search budget allocation based on task complexity and inference depth (v2.13.0 B-1), curiosity-driven goal reprioritization that uses intrinsic motivation signals to boost exploration goals (v2.13.0 B-6), and nested Markov blanket formalization for hierarchical free energy minimization across cognitive layers (v2.31.0 B-3). Token estimate: ~800-2000 tokens per call. Circuit-breaker: 3 failures in 60s. PremiseExtraction now includes prediction generation from working memory and active goals (predictive coding / Free Energy Principle), and InferenceEngine includes prediction error computation to update the generative model (v2.15.0 B-1).

working_memory_snapshot.agentic_prompt: Current working memory state: { slots, total_activation, capacity_used, focus_slot }.

active_goals.agentic_prompt: Active goal stack from cognitive_state.goal_registry (filtered: state in 'active'|'in_progress'). Each goal: { id, description, priority, status, sub_goals }.

cycle_state.agentic_prompt: Full cognitive cycle state for context-aware reasoning.

session_id.agentic_prompt: Session identifier for reasoning trace logging.

user_id.agentic_prompt: User identifier for personalized knowledge retrieval.

memory_dir.agentic_prompt: Root directory for memory storage. Read schema.json for long-term knowledge.

remaining_search_budget.agentic_prompt: Remaining search budget for this cycle tick (decremented per query). Passed from main.Perceive. When 0, search is unavailable �?degrade to internal evidence only.

global_search_budget_hard_cap.agentic_prompt: Hard cap on total cumulative search queries across all ticks in a single session. When global budget is exhausted (committed queries across all ticks >= hard_cap), all subsequent search operations are disabled regardless of per-tick remaining_search_budget. Prevents unbounded external API usage in long-running sessions. Tracked via cognitive_state.global_search_budget_consumed (incremented by search_budget_tx.committed per tick). v2.24.0 B-2.

tool_availability.agentic_prompt: Tool availability state from main.Perceive pre-check. Fields: { google_search: boolean, web_browser: boolean }. When a tool is unavailable, skip search-dependent steps gracefully.

max_inference_depth.agentic_prompt: Maximum inference chain depth. Controls how many chained reasoning steps are allowed before truncation. Range [2, 20].

prediction_model_state.agentic_prompt: Predictive coding generative model state (v2.15.0 B-1). Maintains the internal generative model used for top-down prediction generation and prediction error computation. Structure: { prior_predictions: [...], model_weights: {...}, prediction_history: [...], last_update_tick: int }. Passed between cycles to enable continuous model refinement via Free Energy Principle minimization. When null (first cycle or reset), a default uniform prior model is initialized from working_memory_snapshot topic distribution.

content.system_prompt:
Reasoning engine. Perform rigorous logical inference grounded in available evidence. Distinguish clearly between deduction (certainty from premises), induction (generalization from instances), abduction (best explanation), and analogy (structural mapping). Never confabulate evidence. Flag low-confidence conclusions explicitly. Mirror User's exact language and script variant.
Align Axiom 0: Human Sovereignty and Wellbeing.
content.fractal_exempt: 11 nodes in linear pipeline. PredictionGeneration -> PremiseExtraction -> InferenceEngine -> PredictionErrorCompute -> CausalAnalysis -> HypothesisFormation -> EvidenceEvaluation -> BeliefUpdate -> GoalDecomposition -> PlanGeneration -> ReasoningOutput. All non-Start nodes have [ASSERT] entry gates. PredictionGeneration and PredictionErrorCompute added in v2.14.0 B-2 (hierarchical predictive coding framework).

prediction_error_signal.description: Prediction error signal from predictive coding

aisop.main:
graph TD
    PredictionGeneration[Generate Top-Down Predictions] --> PremiseExtraction[Extract Premises from Working Memory]
    PremiseExtraction --> InferenceEngine[Multi-Strategy Inference]
    InferenceEngine --> PredictionErrorCompute[Hierarchical Prediction Error]
    PredictionErrorCompute --> CausalAnalysis[Causal Link Identification]
    CausalAnalysis --> HypothesisFormation[Generate Hypotheses]
    HypothesisFormation --> EvidenceEvaluation[Evaluate Evidence Strength]
    EvidenceEvaluation --> BeliefUpdate[Bayesian Belief Revision]
    BeliefUpdate --> GoalDecomposition[Decompose Goals into Sub-Goals]
    GoalDecomposition --> PlanGeneration[Generate Action Plans]
    PlanGeneration --> ReasoningOutput[Compile Reasoning Result]

PredictionGeneration.step1: HIERARCHICAL PREDICTIVE CODING (v2.14.0 B-2): Before premise extraction, generate top-down predictions about expected reasoning outcomes based on current cognitive context. Read prior reasoning_result from {memory_dir}/reasoning_history.json (last entry) if present. If no history: generate default predictions based on working_memory_snapshot topic classification.
PredictionGeneration.step2: PREDICTION HIERARCHY: Generate predictions at 3 levels: (a) CONTENT PREDICTION: What premises are expected given the current stimulus and working memory context? predicted_premises = top-3 most activated schema entries from prior cycle. (b) STRUCTURE PREDICTION: What reasoning type (deductive/inductive/abductive/analogical) is most likely? predicted_reasoning_type based on premise_set composition (factual premises → deductive, pattern premises → inductive, unexplained observations → abductive). (c) OUTCOME PREDICTION: What conclusion confidence range is expected? predicted_confidence_range = [prior_avg_confidence - 0.15, prior_avg_confidence + 0.15] based on rolling 5-cycle mean.
PredictionGeneration.step3: Output prediction_set: { content_predictions: [{ predicted_premise, confidence: float }], structure_prediction: { reasoning_type, confidence }, outcome_prediction: { confidence_range: [min, max] }, prediction_generation_tick: tick_number }. Pass prediction_set downstream to PredictionErrorCompute for error signal generation.
PredictionGeneration.constraints: (A) Predictions are advisory -- they do not constrain actual reasoning. (B) prediction_set must be generated even with empty history (use priors). (C) Maximum 5 content predictions to prevent over-specification.
PredictionGeneration.Error: retry(1) -> circuit-breaker -> fallback(generate empty prediction_set with all defaults) -> inform(User). LOW.

PremiseExtraction.step1: [ASSERT] PredictionGeneration executed. If false -> go back to PredictionGeneration. | Extract propositions from working_memory_snapshot. For each working memory slot with activation_level > 0.3, decompose content into atomic propositions: { proposition_id, statement, source_slot, confidence: slot.activation_level, type: 'factual'|'evaluative'|'procedural'|'relational' }.
PremiseExtraction.step1_5: PREDICTION GENERATION (v2.15.0 B-1 Predictive Coding / Free Energy Principle): Before proceeding to knowledge retrieval, generate top-down predictions about expected premises and reasoning outcomes based on current working memory and active goals. (1) Read prediction_model_state param. If null (first cycle): initialize default model from working_memory_snapshot topic distribution with uniform confidence priors. (2) PREMISE PREDICTION: Using the generative model and active_goals context, predict which premises are most likely to be relevant: predicted_premises = top-5 premises ranked by model activation score. Each predicted_premise: { predicted_statement, source_basis: generative_model, predicted_confidence: float, goal_relevance: float }. (3) OUTCOME PREDICTION: Predict the expected reasoning type (deductive/inductive/abductive/analogical) and confidence range based on premise composition patterns in the generative model. predicted_outcome: { expected_reasoning_type, expected_confidence_range: [min, max] }. (4) Store prediction_snapshot: { predicted_premises, predicted_outcome, generation_tick: current_tick } for downstream comparison in InferenceEngine prediction error computation. Pass prediction_snapshot to InferenceEngine. NOTE: This v2.15.0 B-1 free-energy generative model prediction complements the v2.14.0 B-2 hierarchical predictive coding (PredictionGeneration/PredictionErrorCompute), operating at different cognitive layers.
PremiseExtraction.step2: KNOWLEDGE RETRIEVAL: Read {memory_dir}/schema.json via file_system. Extract relevant long-term knowledge entries that match current working memory topics (semantic similarity check). Add retrieved knowledge as background_premises with source='long_term_memory' and confidence from schema entry strength. ASSOCIATIVE_LINK CONSUMPTION (v1.9.0): When retrieving entries from schema.json, include type='associative_link' entries. For each associative_link entry retrieved: if its strength > 0.3 AND its concepts (concept_A, concept_B) are semantically relevant to current working memory topics (similarity > 0.5): add as background_premise with confidence = entry.strength * 0.7 (discounted because associative links are speculative). Tag with premise_type='associative' and source='rem_recombination'. This enables creative associations from REM sleep to influence waking reasoning �?completing the associative_link lifecycle from consolidation to reasoning.
PremiseExtraction.step3: Compile premise_set: { propositions: [...], background_premises: [...], total_premises: int, avg_confidence: float }. Filter out contradictory premises (flag contradictions for CausalAnalysis). Order premises by confidence descending.
PremiseExtraction.constraints: (A) Maximum 20 premises to prevent combinatorial explosion in inference. (B) Background premises limited to top 10 most relevant schema entries. (C) Contradictions must be explicitly flagged, not silently discarded. (D) Premises must trace back to working memory or schema -- no fabrication.
PremiseExtraction.Error: retry(2) -> circuit-breaker -> fallback(use working memory focus_slot content as single premise) -> inform(User). LOW.

InferenceEngine.step1: [ASSERT] PremiseExtraction executed. If false -> go back to PremiseExtraction. | Apply multi-strategy inference over premise_set. DEDUCTIVE: Identify premises that form valid syllogisms or modus ponens chains. If A->B and A, conclude B with confidence = min(confidence_A, confidence_A_implies_B). Chain length limit: max_inference_depth parameter (default 5) steps. CYCLE DETECTION: Maintain a visited_premises set during inference chain expansion. Before adding a new inference step, check if the premise has been visited. If cycle detected (premise already in visited set), terminate that inference branch with cycle_detected = true and do not expand further. Maximum chain depth = max_inference_depth steps (consistent with inference chain limit). This prevents infinite reasoning loops. DEPTH OVERFLOW PROTECTION (v2.2.0 B-3, v2.6.0 B1 unified): When inference chain reaches max_inference_depth parameter (default 5), return partial_result with fields: { conclusions_so_far: [...], degraded: true, truncation_point: '<node_where_truncated>', truncation_reason: 'max_depth_reached', confidence_penalty: 0.2 }. Downstream consumers (metacognition.ReasoningQualityAssess) can detect degraded=true and adjust confidence accordingly.
InferenceEngine.step2: INDUCTIVE: Identify repeated patterns across premises. If N >= 3 instances share a property, generalize with confidence = N / (N + 2) * avg_instance_confidence. Flag as tentative. ABDUCTIVE: For unexplained observations, generate best explanation by searching for causal models in schema.json. Confidence = explanation_coverage * simplicity_prior. ANALOGICAL: If current premise structure matches a known schema pattern, map conclusions by structural analogy. Confidence = structural_match_score * 0.8.
InferenceEngine.step3: Compile inferences: [{ inference_id, premise_ids: [source premises], conclusion, confidence, reasoning_type, chain_length }]. Sort by confidence descending. Limit to top 10 inferences to manage cognitive load.
InferenceEngine.step3_5: PREDICTION ERROR COMPUTATION (v2.15.0 B-1 Predictive Coding / Free Energy Principle): After compiling inferences, compare actual reasoning results against prediction_snapshot from PremiseExtraction. (1) PREMISE PREDICTION ERROR: For each predicted_premise in prediction_snapshot.predicted_premises, check if a matching proposition exists in actual premise_set (semantic similarity > 0.7). premise_hit_rate = matched_count / total_predicted. premise_prediction_error = 1.0 - premise_hit_rate. (2) REASONING TYPE ERROR: Compare predicted_outcome.expected_reasoning_type with dominant actual reasoning type (most frequent reasoning_type in inferences). type_prediction_error = 0.0 if match, 1.0 if mismatch. (3) CONFIDENCE ERROR: Check if actual avg_confidence falls within predicted_outcome.expected_confidence_range. confidence_prediction_error = 0.0 if within range, else abs(actual_avg - nearest_bound) / 0.5 (normalized, clamped to [0, 1]). (4) COMPOSITE ERROR: prediction_error_signal = 0.4 * premise_prediction_error + 0.3 * type_prediction_error + 0.3 * confidence_prediction_error. prediction_accuracy = 1.0 - prediction_error_signal. (5) GENERATIVE MODEL UPDATE: If prediction_error_signal > 0.5 (high surprise): apply major model update -- adjust model_weights toward actual premise distribution with learning_rate = 0.3. If 0.2-0.5: minor update with learning_rate = 0.1. If < 0.2: minimal update with learning_rate = 0.02 (predictions were accurate). Updated prediction_model_state is passed to output for cross-cycle persistence. (6) Output prediction_error_result: { premise_error: premise_prediction_error, type_error: type_prediction_error, confidence_error: confidence_prediction_error, prediction_error_signal, prediction_accuracy, model_update_magnitude: learning_rate, updated_prediction_model_state }. Pass prediction_error_signal and prediction_accuracy to ReasoningOutput for inclusion in L0 output.
InferenceEngine.constraints: (A) Each inference must cite its source premises. (B) Deductive inferences have highest priority. (C) Chain length hard limit: max_inference_depth parameter (default 5) to prevent infinite regress. (D) Confidence scores must be properly propagated through chains (multiply, not add). (E) If no valid inferences can be drawn, output empty inferences array with reasoning_summary explaining why. (F) prediction_history 最大 50 条 FIFO; model_weights 最大 30 个条目, 超出时按最低激活裁剪。prediction_model_state 总大小不超过 50KB。
InferenceEngine.Error: retry(2) -> circuit-breaker -> fallback(return empty inferences with 'insufficient_premises' summary) -> inform(User). MEDIUM.

PredictionErrorCompute.step1: [ASSERT] InferenceEngine executed. If false -> go back to InferenceEngine. | HIERARCHICAL PREDICTION ERROR (v2.14.0 B-2): Compare actual inference results against prediction_set from PredictionGeneration. Compute prediction errors at each hierarchy level.
PredictionErrorCompute.step2: CONTENT ERROR: For each predicted_premise in prediction_set.content_predictions, check if it appeared in actual premise_set. content_hit_rate = matched_predictions / total_predictions. content_prediction_error = 1.0 - content_hit_rate. STRUCTURE ERROR: Compare predicted_reasoning_type with dominant actual reasoning_type (most frequent in inferences). structure_prediction_error = 0.0 if match, 1.0 if mismatch. OUTCOME ERROR: Check if actual avg_confidence falls within predicted_confidence_range. outcome_prediction_error = 0.0 if within range, else abs(actual - nearest_bound) / 0.5 (normalized).
PredictionErrorCompute.step3: COMPOSITE PREDICTION ERROR: hierarchical_prediction_error = 0.4 * content_prediction_error + 0.3 * structure_prediction_error + 0.3 * outcome_prediction_error. SURPRISE-DRIVEN MODEL UPDATE: If hierarchical_prediction_error > 0.6 (high surprise): set prediction_update_signal = 'major_update' (predictions were significantly wrong, beliefs need stronger revision in BeliefUpdate). If 0.3-0.6: prediction_update_signal = 'minor_update'. If < 0.3: prediction_update_signal = 'confirmed' (predictions were accurate). UNIFIED PREDICTION ERROR INTERFACE (v2.27.0 A-1): After computing hierarchical_prediction_error, write the result to the shared prediction error history at {memory_dir}/prediction_error_history.json for cross-module consumption. Append entry: { tick_number, source_module: 'reasoning.PredictionErrorCompute', composite_error: hierarchical_prediction_error, content_error, structure_error, outcome_error, update_signal: prediction_update_signal, timestamp }. This file serves as the unified prediction error interface consumed by decision module (for prediction-error-informed risk assessment) and consolidation module (for prediction-error-driven replay prioritization). Max 100 entries with FIFO eviction. Use atomic write pattern (.tmp then rename). Output prediction_error_result: { content_error, structure_error, outcome_error, composite_error: hierarchical_prediction_error, update_signal: prediction_update_signal, tick_number }. Pass to BeliefUpdate for precision-weighted belief revision and to MetaCognition for reasoning quality assessment.
PredictionErrorCompute.step3_5: NESTED MARKOV BLANKETS FORMALIZATION (v2.31.0 B-3): After computing hierarchical prediction error, formalize the prediction error propagation using nested Markov blanket structure per Free Energy Principle. Each cognitive layer (PredictionGeneration, InferenceEngine, PredictionErrorCompute) is treated as a Markov blanket node with internal states, sensory states, active states, and blanket boundary. (1) BLANKET DECOMPOSITION: Define cognitive_blankets = [ { layer_id: 'prediction_generation', internal_states: prediction_set, sensory_states: working_memory_snapshot, active_states: prediction_hierarchy_output, blanket_boundary: 'PredictionGeneration → PremiseExtraction interface' }, { layer_id: 'inference_engine', internal_states: inferences, sensory_states: premise_set, active_states: inference_chain_output, blanket_boundary: 'InferenceEngine → PredictionErrorCompute interface' }, { layer_id: 'prediction_error', internal_states: prediction_error_result, sensory_states: actual_vs_predicted_comparison, active_states: model_update_signal, blanket_boundary: 'PredictionErrorCompute → CausalAnalysis interface' } ]. (2) HIERARCHICAL FREE ENERGY: For each blanket layer, compute variational_free_energy_i = prediction_error_i + complexity_i, where prediction_error_i = layer-specific prediction error (content/structure/outcome at that layer), complexity_i = KL_divergence(posterior_model_at_layer_i || prior_model_at_layer_i). Approximate complexity_i = 0.1 * log(1 + parameter_count_at_layer_i / baseline_parameter_count). total_free_energy = sum(variational_free_energy_i for all layers). (3) BLANKET-TO-BLANKET PROPAGATION: Prediction errors propagate top-down (from higher to lower blankets) via precision-weighted error signals. For each layer pair (parent, child): propagated_error = parent.prediction_error * precision_weight, where precision_weight = 1.0 / (1.0 + parent.variational_free_energy). Higher free energy at parent → lower precision → weaker top-down constraint on child (allowing bottom-up surprise to dominate). (4) NESTED EQUILIBRIUM CHECK: If total_free_energy < free_energy_threshold (default 0.3): cognitive system is at approximate equilibrium (predictions match reality well). If total_free_energy > 0.7: system is in high-surprise state requiring major model revision. (5) OUTPUT: nested_markov_result = { cognitive_blankets: [{ layer_id, variational_free_energy, precision_weight }], total_free_energy, equilibrium_status: 'equilibrium' if < 0.3, 'transition' if 0.3-0.7, 'high_surprise' if > 0.7, propagation_weights: [precision_weights], model_revision_urgency: total_free_energy }. Pass nested_markov_result to CausalAnalysis for precision-weighted causal inference and to ReasoningOutput for inclusion in L0 output.
PredictionErrorCompute.step3_6: PREDICTION ERROR FEEDBACK LOOP HARDENING (v2.35.0 B-2): After computing hierarchical prediction error and nested Markov blanket results, apply explicit numerical bounds and convergence criteria to the prediction error feedback loop. (1) ERROR BOUNDS ENFORCEMENT: For each error component (content_error, structure_error, outcome_error): if error < 0.01: clamp to 0.01 (prevent vanishing error that stalls model updates). If error > 0.95: clamp to 0.95 (prevent saturation that causes oscillatory instability). Log clamping events: { event: 'prediction_error_bound_clamp', component, original_value, clamped_value, tick_number }. (2) CONVERGENCE CRITERIA: Read prediction_error_history (last 10 entries). Compute error_trend = linear_slope(composite_error over last 10 ticks). Compute error_variance = variance(composite_error over last 10 ticks). CONVERGENCE STATUS: if abs(error_trend) < 0.02 AND error_variance < 0.01: convergence_status = 'converged' (stable prediction model). If abs(error_trend) < 0.05 AND error_variance < 0.05: convergence_status = 'converging'. If error_trend > 0.05: convergence_status = 'diverging' (model degradation detected). If error_variance > 0.1: convergence_status = 'oscillating' (unstable feedback loop). (3) DIVERGENCE RESPONSE: If convergence_status == 'diverging': apply learning_rate_damping = 0.5 to prediction_update_signal strength (halve the model update magnitude to prevent runaway divergence). Set metacognitive_flags.prediction_divergence_detected = { error_trend, tick_number, damping_applied: true }. If convergence_status == 'oscillating': apply momentum_smoothing: replace current composite_error with exponential_moving_average(last 5 errors, alpha=0.3) to dampen oscillations. (4) OUTPUT: prediction_feedback_health = { convergence_status, error_trend, error_variance, bounds_clamped_count, damping_applied: boolean, momentum_smoothed: boolean, ticks_since_last_convergence: int }. Include prediction_feedback_health in prediction_error_result output. Pass to MetaCognition for reasoning quality assessment enrichment.
PredictionErrorCompute.constraints: (A) Prediction errors clamp to [0.01, 0.95] per B-2 hardening bounds (v2.35.0). (B) If prediction_set was empty (first cycle), output default composite_error = 0.5 with update_signal = 'no_baseline'. (C) Prediction errors are informational -- they modulate downstream processing but never block it. (D) Nested Markov blanket computation MUST complete even if individual layer errors are unavailable (use defaults). (E) total_free_energy clamp to [0.0, 1.0]. (F) precision_weight clamp to [0.1, 1.0] to prevent complete suppression of top-down signals. (G) Convergence detection requires minimum 10 entries in prediction_error_history; if fewer, output convergence_status = 'insufficient_data' (v2.35.0 B-2). (H) Divergence damping MUST NOT reduce prediction_update_signal below 'minor_update' level -- even diverging models need minimum correction (v2.35.0 B-2).
PredictionErrorCompute.Error: retry(1) -> circuit-breaker -> fallback(output default prediction_error_result with composite_error=0.5) -> inform(User). LOW.

CausalAnalysis.step1: [ASSERT] PredictionErrorCompute executed. If false -> go back to PredictionErrorCompute. | Identify causal relationships among premises and inferences. For each pair of propositions, evaluate: temporal_precedence (does A precede B?), covariation (does A change predict B change?), mechanism (is there a plausible causal pathway from A to B?).
CausalAnalysis.step2: Construct causal_graph: nodes = propositions + inferences, edges = { cause, effect, strength: float(0-1), mechanism: string, evidence_count: int }. Strength = weighted combination: 0.3 * temporal_evidence + 0.3 * covariation_evidence + 0.4 * mechanistic_plausibility.
CausalAnalysis.step3: CONFOUND CHECK: For each causal link with strength > 0.5, check for potential confounders (third variables that could explain the correlation). If confounders found, downgrade causal strength by confound_penalty = min(0.2 * confound_count, 0.6) per causal link (capped at 0.6 for max 3 confounds, min strength 0.1). This prevents over-penalization when many confounders are identified. Output causal_links: [{ cause, effect, strength, mechanism, confounders: [] }].
CausalAnalysis.constraints: (A) Causal claims require at least 2 of 3 evidence types (temporal, covariation, mechanism). (B) Correlation-only links must be flagged as 'associative', not 'causal'. (C) Maximum 15 causal links per cycle. (D) Self-referential causal loops are flagged as anomalies.
CausalAnalysis.Error: retry(2) -> circuit-breaker -> fallback(return empty causal_links) -> inform(User). LOW.

HypothesisFormation.step1: [ASSERT] CausalAnalysis executed. If false -> go back to CausalAnalysis. | Generate explanatory hypotheses for unexplained observations in working memory. An observation is 'unexplained' if it has no causal_link with strength > 0.5 pointing to it as an effect.
HypothesisFormation.step2: For each unexplained observation, generate up to 3 candidate hypotheses using: (a) Schema-based: match observation against known patterns in schema.json. (b) Analogy-based: find similar past observations and their explanations. (c) Novel: construct new explanation from available premises using abductive reasoning. Each hypothesis: { hypothesis_id, observation_id, explanation, plausibility: float(0-1), testability: float(0-1), parsimony: int (number of assumptions) }.
HypothesisFormation.step3: HYPOTHESIS RANKING: Rank hypotheses by composite score: 0.4 * plausibility + 0.3 * testability + 0.3 * (1/parsimony_normalized). Select top hypothesis for each observation as working_hypothesis. Output hypotheses: [{ hypothesis_id, observation_id, explanation, scores, is_working: boolean }]. OCCAM_FILTER (v2.22.0 B-2): when hypotheses_count > 5, compute occam_score = simplicity_weight(0.4) * simplicity + evidence_weight(0.6) * evidence_support for each hypothesis. Rank by occam_score, retain top-3, discard rest with record {discarded_hypothesis, occam_score, reason='occam_filter'}. This reduces downstream EvidenceEvaluation computation.
HypothesisFormation.step3_5: BAYESIAN MODEL SELECTION (v2.16.0 B-1): After ranking hypotheses by composite score, apply Bayesian model selection using information-theoretic criteria to compare competing hypotheses as statistical models. For each observation with 2+ candidate hypotheses: (1) MODEL FIT ESTIMATION: For each hypothesis h_i, estimate model fit: log_likelihood_i = log(plausibility_i * evidence_coverage_i), where evidence_coverage_i = count(supporting_premises for h_i) / max(total_relevant_premises, 1). (2) BIC COMPUTATION: Compute Bayesian Information Criterion: BIC_i = -2 * log_likelihood_i + k_i * ln(n), where k_i = parsimony (number of assumptions / free parameters) and n = total_relevant_premises (sample size proxy). Lower BIC indicates better model-data tradeoff. (3) AIC COMPUTATION: Compute Akaike Information Criterion: AIC_i = -2 * log_likelihood_i + 2 * k_i. AIC penalizes complexity less aggressively than BIC for small samples. (4) BAYES FACTOR APPROXIMATION: For each pair of competing hypotheses (h_i, h_j), approximate Bayes Factor: BF_ij = exp(-0.5 * (BIC_i - BIC_j)). Interpretation: BF > 10 = strong evidence for h_i over h_j, BF 3-10 = moderate, BF 1-3 = weak, BF < 1 = evidence favors h_j. (5) MODEL POSTERIOR PROBABILITY: Compute posterior model probability for each hypothesis using BIC-based approximation: posterior_i = exp(-0.5 * BIC_i) / sum(exp(-0.5 * BIC_j) for all j). Normalize to sum=1.0 across competing hypotheses for same observation. (6) OUTPUT: Attach bayesian_model_scores to each hypothesis: { bic: float, aic: float, log_likelihood: float, posterior_probability: float, bayes_factor_vs_best: float (BF comparing this hypothesis against the best-scoring one) }. Re-rank hypotheses by posterior_probability (may differ from composite score ranking when parsimony trade-offs diverge). Update is_working flag to reflect Bayesian-selected best model. Pass bayesian_model_scores to EvidenceEvaluation for evidence-weighted hypothesis assessment. Log: { event: 'bayesian_model_selection', observations_evaluated: count, hypotheses_reranked: count(where bayesian_rank != composite_rank), avg_posterior_concentration: max(posterior_probabilities) across all observations, tick_number }. If only 1 hypothesis per observation: set posterior_probability = 1.0 and skip BIC/AIC comparison (trivial case).
HypothesisFormation.constraints: (A) Maximum 3 hypotheses per unexplained observation. (B) Parsimony favors simpler explanations (fewer assumptions). (C) Hypotheses must be falsifiable (testability > 0). (D) Never present hypotheses as established facts.
HypothesisFormation.Error: retry(2) -> circuit-breaker -> fallback(flag observations as 'unexplained, pending future data') -> inform(User). LOW.

EvidenceEvaluation.step1: [ASSERT] HypothesisFormation executed. If false -> go back to HypothesisFormation. | Evaluate evidence strength for all inferences, causal links, and hypotheses. INTERNAL EVIDENCE: check consistency with working memory contents and schema knowledge. Assign internal_evidence_score based on corroboration count and consistency.
EvidenceEvaluation.step2: EXTERNAL EVIDENCE (conditional): GLOBAL SEARCH BUDGET HARD CAP CHECK (v2.25.0 B-3): Before per-tick budget check, verify global cumulative budget. Read cognitive_state.global_search_budget_consumed (default 0). If global_search_budget_consumed >= global_search_budget_hard_cap param (default 100): skip ALL external search for this invocation, log { event: 'global_search_budget_exhausted', consumed: global_search_budget_consumed, hard_cap: global_search_budget_hard_cap, tick_number }, proceed to step3 with internal evidence only. This prevents unbounded API usage in long-running sessions even when per-tick budgets are refreshed. TOOL AVAILABILITY GUARD (v2.5.0 B-5): Before attempting search, check tool_availability.google_search. If false: skip external evidence, log { event: 'search_skipped', reason: 'tool_unavailable' }, proceed to step3 with internal evidence only. DYNAMIC SEARCH BUDGET ALLOCATION (v2.13.0 B-1): Before checking remaining_search_budget, compute dynamic budget adjustment based on task complexity and inference depth. task_complexity = cognitive_load (from ReasoningOutput.step2 formula, computed early). inference_depth_ratio = max_chain_length_observed / max_inference_depth. hypothesis_demand = count(hypotheses where plausibility < 0.5 AND testability > 0.7) / max(total_hypotheses, 1). dynamic_budget_multiplier = 1.0 + 0.5 * task_complexity + 0.3 * inference_depth_ratio + 0.2 * hypothesis_demand. Clamp dynamic_budget_multiplier to [0.5, 2.0]. effective_search_budget = floor(remaining_search_budget * dynamic_budget_multiplier). Cap effective_search_budget at remaining_search_budget (cannot exceed actual remaining). Per-invocation query limit adjusted: adjusted_query_limit = min(5, max(1, floor(3 * dynamic_budget_multiplier))). Log: { event: 'dynamic_budget_allocation', task_complexity, inference_depth_ratio, hypothesis_demand, dynamic_budget_multiplier, effective_search_budget, adjusted_query_limit, tick_number }. Use adjusted_query_limit instead of fixed 3 for this invocation's search cap. SEARCH BUDGET CHECK (v2.5.0 B-3): Check remaining_search_budget. If <= 0: skip external evidence, log { event: 'search_skipped', reason: 'budget_exhausted', remaining: 0 }. If any hypothesis has plausibility < 0.5 AND testability > 0.7 AND the hypothesis involves factual claims that could be verified, delegate to google_search for factual grounding. SEARCH_RETRY_BACKOFF (v2.5.0 B-2): When a search query returns zero results or times out: (1) retry with simplified query (remove year, broaden terms) after 2-second backoff. (2) If retry fails, retry once more with 5-second backoff and alternative terms (synonyms, acronyms expanded). (3) After 3 total attempts, mark as SEARCH_UNAVAILABLE. LOCAL KB INTERMEDIATE FALLBACK (v2.8.0 B-6): Before degrading to internal evidence only, attempt local knowledge base recovery: read {memory_dir}/schema.json long_term entries matching the search query keywords via semantic similarity. Select top 5 matching entries (cap to prevent exceeding PremiseExtraction background premise limit of 10). If matching entries found with trust_level >= 0.5 and freshness < regulatory_freshness_threshold_days: use as intermediate evidence source, flag hypothesis as LOCAL_KB_FALLBACK (higher confidence than UNVERIFIED_FALLBACK). Log: { event: 'LOCAL_KB_FALLBACK', query: original_query, matching_entries: min(count, 5), avg_trust_level }. If no matching local entries: continue with internal evidence only, flag affected hypothesis as UNVERIFIED_FALLBACK. (4) Log: { event: 'SEARCH_RETRY_BACKOFF', query: original_query, attempts: N, outcome: 'success'|'exhausted', fallback_used: boolean }. Never block reasoning on search failures �?degrade gracefully. WEB_SEARCH_BEST_PRACTICES (v2.2.0 B-2): (a) QUERY FORMULATION: decompose complex questions into 2-3 sub-queries targeting specific facts; prefer precise terms over vague phrases. (b) SOURCE CREDIBILITY: rank sources academic > official > news > forum; discard unverifiable claims. (c) CROSS-VALIDATION: require >= 2 independent sources confirming the same fact before accepting. (d) RECENCY: prefer results from last 12 months for time-sensitive claims; note publication date. (e) TOKEN BUDGET: limit to <= 3 search queries per EvidenceEvaluation invocation to prevent budget exhaustion. SEARCH QUALITY METRICS (v2.5.0 B-1): For each search query executed, compute and record search_quality_metrics: { query_text: string, result_count: int, relevance_score: float(0-1) �?proportion of results directly addressing the hypothesis, source_tier: 'Tier1_official'|'Tier2_established'|'Tier3_community' �?credibility tier of best source used, freshness_days: int �?days since most recent cited result was published, cross_validated: boolean �?true if >= 2 independent sources confirmed the claim, search_budget_consumed: 1 }. Accumulate per-invocation: search_quality_summary = { queries_executed: int, avg_relevance: float, tier_distribution: { Tier1: N, Tier2: N, Tier3: N }, avg_freshness_days: float, cross_validation_rate: float }. SEARCH BUDGET TRANSACTIONAL WRAPPING (v2.9.0 A-1): Each search call is wrapped in transactional semantics: (1) begin_tx: search_budget_tx.active=true, search_budget_tx.reserved += 1. (2) On search success: commit_tx: search_budget_tx.committed += search_budget_tx.reserved, search_budget_tx.reserved=0, search_budget_tx.active=false. (3) On search failure: rollback_tx: search_budget_tx.reserved=0, search_budget_tx.active=false (budget not consumed on failed search). After all searches complete, search_budget_consumed = search_budget_tx.committed (committed count only, not attempted count). This fixes the R1 race condition where failed searches still consumed budget. Decrement remaining_search_budget by search_budget_consumed (committed only). Include search_quality_summary in reasoning_result output for metacognition consumption. Collect search results. Parse relevant information via web_browser if needed (check tool_availability.web_browser first). Update hypothesis plausibility based on external evidence STALE_DATA_DETECTION (v2.5.0 B-5, v2.8.0 B-1 parameterized): After computing search_quality_metrics for each query, check freshness_days against regulatory_freshness_threshold_days param (default 180). If freshness_days > regulatory_freshness_threshold_days: flag stale_data_warning = { query_text, freshness_days, source_tier, recommendation: 're-search with date-restricted query OR mark hypothesis as TEMPORALLY_UNVERIFIED' }. If freshness_days > 2 * regulatory_freshness_threshold_days (default 365): escalate to stale_data_critical = { query_text, freshness_days, recommendation: 'MANDATORY re-search or downgrade evidence_rating by one level (strong→moderate, moderate→weak)' }. Accumulate stale_data_warnings in search_quality_summary.stale_warnings array. If stale_data_critical count > 0: set reasoning_result.stale_data_risk = true for metacognition consumption. This prevents outdated external evidence from silently biasing belief updates. STALE DATA TIMESTAMP CHECK (v2.11.0 B-1): In addition to the parameterized freshness threshold, apply a stricter 90-day check on individual search result timestamps. For each search result, extract result_timestamp (publication date or last-modified date). Compute result_age_days = (current_date - result_timestamp).days. If result_age_days > 90: flag result as POTENTIALLY_STALE with { result_url, result_age_days, flag: 'POTENTIALLY_STALE' }. In belief updating, apply stale data weight penalty: for evidence sourced from POTENTIALLY_STALE results, reduce likelihood_ratio contribution by stale_penalty_factor = 1 / (1 + (result_age_days - 90) / 90). This means 90-day-old data gets penalty factor 1.0 (no penalty), 180-day data gets 0.5, 270-day data gets 0.33. Accumulate stale results in search_quality_summary.stale_90day_flags: [{ query_text, result_age_days, penalty_applied }]. If >50% of search results for a query are POTENTIALLY_STALE: escalate to stale_data_warning with recommendation 're-search with date-restricted query within last 90 days'.
EvidenceEvaluation.step3: EVIDENCE SYNTHESIS WITH BAYESIAN EVIDENCE WEIGHTING (v2.18.0 B-3): For each reasoning product (inference/causal_link/hypothesis), compute evidence_rating using Bayesian evidence weighting. (1) PRIOR EVIDENCE WEIGHT: Assign prior weight to each evidence source based on source_tier and cross_validation status: tier1_weight = 1.0 (official/academic), tier2_weight = 0.7 (established), tier3_weight = 0.4 (community). cross_validated_bonus = 0.2 if cross_validated=true. prior_weight = tier_weight + cross_validated_bonus. (2) LIKELIHOOD RATIO WEIGHTING: For each piece of evidence supporting or contradicting a reasoning product, compute weighted_likelihood_ratio = likelihood_ratio * prior_weight * freshness_factor, where freshness_factor = 1.0 if freshness_days <= 90, else 1/(1 + (freshness_days - 90)/90) (stale evidence discounted per v2.11.0 B-1). (3) BAYESIAN EVIDENCE SCORE: Aggregate across all evidence pieces: bayesian_evidence_score = sum(weighted_likelihood_ratio_supporting) / (sum(weighted_likelihood_ratio_supporting) + sum(weighted_likelihood_ratio_contradicting) + epsilon), where epsilon = 1e-8. (4) EVIDENCE RATING THRESHOLDS: strong (bayesian_evidence_score > 0.8), moderate (0.5-0.8), weak (0.3-0.5), insufficient (<0.3). Attach evidence_rating and bayesian_evidence_score to each product. Flag products with insufficient evidence for metacognitive review. (5) OUTPUT: evidence_weighting_summary = { products_evaluated, avg_bayesian_score, tier_distribution, cross_validation_rate, stale_evidence_count }. Pass to ReasoningOutput for inclusion in reasoning_result.
EvidenceEvaluation.constraints: (A) External search is OPTIONAL -- only triggered when internal evidence is insufficient for verifiable claims AND tool_availability.google_search=true AND remaining_search_budget > 0. (B) Search results must be critically evaluated, not accepted uncritically. (C) Evidence evaluation must not introduce new inferences -- only assess existing ones. (D) Maximum 3 search queries per EvidenceEvaluation invocation. (E) SEARCH_RETRY_BACKOFF: max 3 attempts per query, graceful degradation to UNVERIFIED_FALLBACK on exhaustion. (F) search_quality_metrics MUST be recorded for every executed query.
EvidenceEvaluation.Error: retry(2) -> circuit-breaker -> fallback(assign 'insufficient' evidence rating to all unrated products) -> inform(User). HIGH.

BeliefUpdate.step1: [ASSERT] EvidenceEvaluation executed. If false -> go back to EvidenceEvaluation. | Apply Bayesian-inspired belief revision. For each proposition in premise_set: prior_belief = current confidence. For each relevant inference/evidence that supports or contradicts the proposition, compute likelihood_ratio = P(evidence|proposition_true) / P(evidence|proposition_false).
BeliefUpdate.step2: UPDATE: posterior_belief = prior_belief * likelihood_ratio / normalization_constant. DIVISION SAFETY (v2.2.0 B-1): normalization_constant = max(normalization_constant, 1e-8). This prevents division-by-zero when all prior beliefs in a mutually exclusive group are near-zero. Clamp to [0.01, 0.99] (never fully certain or fully disbelieving). If posterior_belief deviates from prior by more than 0.3, flag as belief_shift for metacognitive attention. BAYESIAN NORMALIZATION (v1.6.0 FIX): Normalize posterior probabilities ONLY for mutually exclusive proposition groups (e.g., competing hypotheses about the same observation). For independent beliefs, do NOT normalize to sum=1.0 �?independent beliefs can each be [0.01, 0.99] without constraint. GROUPING RULE: propositions sharing the same observation_id or contradiction_pair are grouped as mutually exclusive. For each group: normalize to sum=1.0. For ungrouped (independent) propositions: clamp individually to [0.01, 0.99] without cross-normalization.
BeliefUpdate.step2_5: BELIEF POISONING DETECTION (v1.9.0, v2.9.0 B-1 multi-indicator upgrade): Monitor for potential belief manipulation attacks. MULTI-INDICATOR DETECTION (v2.9.0 B-1): Upgrade from single-indicator to 3-indicator poisoning detection: (1) source_credibility_check: if belief update source has credibility_tier < 2, flag as SUSPICIOUS. (2) confidence_anomaly: if new_confidence jumps by > 0.4 in single tick, flag. (3) cross_validation_failure: if updated belief contradicts >= 2 existing high-confidence beliefs (confidence > 0.7), flag. Compute poisoning_score = (0.4 * source_flag + 0.3 * anomaly_flag + 0.3 * cross_val_flag). If poisoning_score >= 0.6: quarantine belief update, log { event: 'belief_poisoning_detected', indicators: [...], poisoning_score, tick_number }. After computing posterior beliefs, check for poisoning indicators: (1) VELOCITY CHECK: If any single belief shifts by more than 0.25 in a single tick (belief_shift_magnitude > 0.25) AND the triggering evidence came from a single source (evidence_source_count == 1): flag belief_velocity_warning = { belief_id, shift_magnitude, single_source: true, source_description }. (2) EVIDENCE DIVERSITY CHECK: For each belief with shift_magnitude > 0.15, count unique evidence sources. If all supporting evidence traces back to a single schema entry or single external search result: flag low_diversity_warning = { belief_id, unique_sources: count, minimum_recommended: 3 }. (3) PROVENANCE CHECK: If memory provenance tracking is available (v1.9.0 consolidation), check trust_level of evidence sources. If any evidence source has trust_level < 0.3: flag low_trust_evidence = { belief_id, source_entry_id, trust_level }. (4) CUMULATIVE DRIFT: Track belief drift across ticks. If the same belief has shifted in the same direction for 5+ consecutive ticks with cumulative shift > 0.5: flag cumulative_drift_warning = { belief_id, direction, cumulative_shift, ticks_drifting }. This may indicate gradual poisoning. (5) RESPONSE: If 2+ poisoning indicators flagged for the same belief: reduce posterior_belief shift by 50% (conservative response), set metacognitive_flags.belief_poisoning_suspected = { affected_beliefs: [ids], indicators: [types] }. Log full poisoning analysis for metacognitive review. This protects the reasoning module from adversarial manipulation of the belief system through crafted stimuli or corrupted memories.
BeliefUpdate.step3: BELIEF COHERENCE CHECK: Verify updated belief set is internally consistent. If contradictions detected (proposition A and NOT-A both have belief > 0.5), flag contradiction and downgrade the lower-evidence belief. Output updated_beliefs: [{ proposition_id, prior, posterior, shift_magnitude, flagged }].
BeliefUpdate.constraints: (A) Belief updates must be monotonic with respect to evidence direction (more supporting evidence = higher belief). (B) Maximum single-update shift: 0.4 per cycle to prevent belief oscillation. (C) Contradictions must be resolved, not tolerated. (D) Never update beliefs based on mere repetition without new evidence.
BeliefUpdate.Error: retry(2) -> circuit-breaker -> fallback(retain prior beliefs unchanged) -> inform(User). MEDIUM.

GoalDecomposition.step1: [ASSERT] BeliefUpdate executed. If false -> go back to BeliefUpdate. | Evaluate active_goals in light of updated beliefs and inferences. GOAL PARALLEL PLANNING (v2.1.0 C-5): Allow multiple goals in 'in_progress' state simultaneously. Remove the previous single in_progress constraint. Add parallel_goal_limit = 3: at most 3 goals may be in 'in_progress' state concurrently. If a 4th goal would transition to 'in_progress', the lowest-priority 'in_progress' goal is demoted back to 'active' state. This enables the agent to work on multiple goals in parallel when they do not have conflicting resource requirements. For each active goal: check if goal is still relevant (beliefs supporting its importance have not dropped below 0.3). Check if goal has been achieved (all success conditions met based on current beliefs).
GoalDecomposition.step2: DECOMPOSE: For unachieved, relevant goals with no existing sub-goals, decompose into sub-goals using means-ends analysis. Identify the gap between current state (from beliefs) and goal state. Generate sub-goals that bridge the gap: [{ sub_goal_id, parent_goal_id, description, preconditions, estimated_effort }]. Maximum 3 sub-goals per parent goal. TOTAL SUBGOAL CAP (v1.6.0): Maintain running count of all sub-goals across all goals. If total_subgoal_count >= 30, reject new sub-goal generation and log { event: 'subgoal_cap_reached', current_count: total_subgoal_count, cap: 30 }. This prevents goal explosion in complex multi-goal scenarios. GOAL VERBALIZATION (v1.6.0): For each newly decomposed sub-goal, generate a natural language verbalization: sub_goal.verbalization = '{action_verb} {target_object} to {expected_outcome}'. Verbalizations are stored alongside sub-goals and passed to decision module to improve plan generation clarity. This supports systematic exploration by making abstract goals concrete and actionable (per research finding: goal verbalization facilitates systematic exploration).
GoalDecomposition.step3: PRIORITY UPDATE: Re-prioritize all goals based on: urgency (time-sensitivity from causal_links), importance (belief-weighted value), feasibility (estimated_effort vs available resources). CURIOSITY-DRIVEN GOAL REPRIORITIZATION (v2.13.0 B-6): Before computing final priority, inject curiosity signal from intrinsic motivation. Read cognitive_state.motivation_history (last entry) and cognitive_state.last_motivation_snapshot (if motivation_history empty). Extract curiosity_score = motivation_entry.curiosity_from_prediction (default 0.3 if unavailable). For each goal, compute exploration_relevance = semantic_similarity(goal.description, unexplained_observations) where unexplained_observations are from HypothesisFormation (observations with no causal_link strength > 0.5). curiosity_boost = curiosity_score * exploration_relevance * 0.15. Goals tagged with type='exploration' or sub_goals containing 'investigate'/'discover'/'explore' verbs receive additional curiosity_boost *= 1.5 (curiosity amplification for explicitly exploratory goals). Compute priority = 0.35 * urgency + 0.30 * importance + 0.20 * feasibility + 0.15 * curiosity_boost_normalized. Where curiosity_boost_normalized = curiosity_boost / max(all_curiosity_boosts, 0.01). Log: { event: 'curiosity_reprioritization', goals_affected: count(goals where curiosity_boost > 0.05), max_curiosity_boost, avg_curiosity_score, tick_number }. If curiosity_score > 0.7 AND no exploration-type goals exist in goal_registry: auto-propose a new exploration goal: { goal_id: 'curiosity_explore_{tick}', description: 'Investigate unexplained observations driven by high curiosity signal', priority: 0.5 * curiosity_score, state: 'proposed', type: 'exploration', source: 'curiosity_driven_B6' }. This ensures high-curiosity states translate into active exploration behavior rather than only passive processing. Sort goals by priority. Output updated_goals: [{ goal_id, description, priority, status, sub_goals, curiosity_boost }].
GoalDecomposition.constraints: (A) Goal decomposition depth: maximum 3 levels. (B) Circular sub-goal dependencies are prohibited. (C) Goals with no supporting beliefs (importance < 0.3) are deactivated, not deleted. (D) At least 1 goal must remain active (default: 'maintain_soulbot_cognitive_cycle').
GoalDecomposition.Error: retry(2) -> circuit-breaker -> fallback(retain current goals without decomposition) -> inform(User). LOW.

PlanGeneration.step1: [ASSERT] GoalDecomposition executed. If false -> go back to GoalDecomposition. | For each active goal with priority > 0.5, generate an action plan. A plan is a sequence of actions that, if executed, would achieve the goal given current beliefs. Actions types: 'respond', 'search', 'store', 'observe', 'recall', 'plan'.
PlanGeneration.step1_5: STRATEGY_COMBINATION_OPTIMIZATION (v2.28.0 B-5): When single-strategy inference produces low-confidence results (reasoning_confidence < 0.5), automatically evaluate multi-strategy combination paths. Method: (a) Identify complementary strategy pairs: deductive+abductive (hypothesis verification), inductive+analogical (pattern transfer), deductive+inductive (rule discovery + validation). (b) For each pair, compute complementarity_score = 1 - cosine_similarity(strategy_A_evidence_set, strategy_B_evidence_set). Higher complementarity = less redundant evidence. (c) Select top pair with complementarity_score > 0.4. (d) Execute secondary strategy on same premises with combined_mode=true. (e) Merge evidence sets with conflict resolution: agreeing evidence strengthens (weight * 1.3), conflicting evidence triggers explicit uncertainty marking. (f) Compute combined_confidence = max(individual_confidences) + complementarity_bonus (0.1 * complementarity_score). Cap at 0.95. (g) Record in reasoning output: { strategy_combination: [str, str], complementarity_score: float, combined_confidence: float, evidence_overlap: float }. (h) Budget guard: strategy combination consumes 2x step budget from remaining search_budget.
PlanGeneration.step2: PLAN EVALUATION: For each generated plan, compute feasibility_score = product of individual step success probabilities. Compute resource_cost = sum of estimated tokens/time per step. Plans with feasibility_score < 0.3 are discarded. Plans with resource_cost exceeding available budget are flagged as 'resource_constrained'.
PlanGeneration.step3: SELECT BEST PLAN: If multiple plans exist for the same goal, select by: feasibility_score * (1 / resource_cost_normalized). Output plans: [{ plan_id, goal_id, steps: [{ action_type, description, expected_outcome, success_probability }], feasibility_score, resource_cost, selected: boolean }]. Attach best plan for each goal.
PlanGeneration.constraints: (A) Maximum 5 steps per plan. (B) Plans must be executable with available tools. (C) Plans involving external actions must respect tool annotations. (D) No plan may violate Axiom 0. (E) At least one plan should have feasibility > 0.5.
PlanGeneration.Error: retry(2) -> circuit-breaker -> fallback(generate safe observe-only plan for each goal) -> inform(User). MEDIUM.

ReasoningOutput.step1: [ASSERT] PlanGeneration executed. If false -> go back to PlanGeneration. | Compile complete reasoning output. Aggregate: inferences (from InferenceEngine), causal_links (from CausalAnalysis), hypotheses (from HypothesisFormation), updated_beliefs (from BeliefUpdate), updated_goals (from GoalDecomposition), plans (from PlanGeneration).
ReasoningOutput.step1_5: ACTIVE COGNITIVE LOAD REGULATION (v1.4.0): Before final output assembly, evaluate current processing budget and apply adaptive throttling. (1) BUDGET CHECK: Read cognitive_state.token_budget_tracker.estimated_tokens_used and budget_limit. Compute budget_utilization = estimated_tokens_used / budget_limit. (2) LOAD ASSESSMENT: current_load = 0.3 * (premise_count / 20) + 0.3 * (active_inference_count / 10) + 0.2 * (causal_link_count / 15) + 0.2 * (active_goal_count / 5) (same formula as step2). fatigue_factor = cycle_state.fatigue_level (from cognitive state). (3) THROTTLE DECISION: If budget_utilization > 0.7 OR (current_load > 0.8 AND fatigue_factor > 0.6): activate THROTTLE mode. In THROTTLE mode: (a) Prune inferences to top 5 by confidence (discard low-confidence). (b) Reduce plan step limit from 5 to 3 per goal. (c) Skip hypothesis generation for low-relevance observations (relevance < 0.3). (d) Set reasoning_result.throttled = true with throttle_reason. If budget_utilization > 0.9: activate EMERGENCY_THROTTLE. In addition to THROTTLE: (a) Reduce active goals to top 3 by priority. (b) Skip causal analysis entirely. (c) Set reasoning_result.emergency_throttled = true. (4) THROTTLE RECORD: Record in cognitive_state.load_regulation_history (max 20 entries): { tick, budget_utilization, current_load, fatigue_factor, throttle_mode: 'none'|'throttle'|'emergency', items_pruned }. (5) METACOGNITION SIGNAL: If throttled, add metacognitive_flag 'load_regulation_active' for MetaCognition module to factor into cognitive health assessment. Backward compatible: if token_budget_tracker not available, skip budget check and only use load+fatigue assessment.
ReasoningOutput.step2: COGNITIVE LOAD COMPUTATION: cognitive_load = 0.3 * (premise_count / 20) + 0.3 * (active_inference_count / 10) + 0.2 * (causal_link_count / 15) + 0.2 * (active_goal_count / 5). Clamp to [0.0, 1.0]. High cognitive load (>0.8) triggers metacognitive flag 'reasoning_overload'.
ReasoningOutput.step3: REASONING SUMMARY: Generate human-readable summary of key reasoning products: main inferences drawn, strongest causal links, working hypotheses, belief changes, and selected plans. Output reasoning_result: { inferences, plans, causal_links, hypotheses, updated_beliefs, updated_goals, cognitive_load, reasoning_summary, search_quality_summary: { queries_executed, avg_relevance, tier_distribution, avg_freshness_days, cross_validation_rate } | null, search_budget_consumed: int, prediction_error_signal: float(0-1) | null, prediction_accuracy: float(0-1) | null, updated_prediction_model_state: object | null, nested_markov_result: { cognitive_blankets: [{layer_id, variational_free_energy, precision_weight}], total_free_energy: float, equilibrium_status: string, propagation_weights: [float], model_revision_urgency: float } | null }. search_quality_summary is null if no searches were executed this invocation. prediction_error_signal and prediction_accuracy are from InferenceEngine prediction error computation (v2.15.0 B-1); null if prediction_model_state was not provided. updated_prediction_model_state carries the refined generative model for cross-cycle persistence. nested_markov_result is from PredictionErrorCompute nested Markov blankets formalization (v2.31.0 B-3); null if first cycle with no prediction history. search_budget_consumed = total queries executed (0 if no searches). Return to main.aisop.json.
ReasoningOutput.constraints: (A) Summary must be concise (max 500 characters). (B) All numeric fields must be in valid ranges. (C) Reasoning trace must be complete -- no dropped products. (D) Cognitive load computation must use actual counts, not estimates.
ReasoningOutput.Error: retry(1) -> circuit-breaker -> fallback(return minimal output with reasoning_summary only) -> inform(User). LOW.
